864.t: The instruments he plays: clarinet, saxophone, trumpet, bass
864.s: He started on clarinet, moved through saxophones and trumpet, and became a bass player for the Eureka band after one lesson from Professor Delmore.
864.q: Well, I first started on clarinet. Mm-hmm. Then saxophones began coming out and fellas induced me to try to get a saxophone. But after I got the saxophone, I wanted to be a trumpet, which I wanted to be a trumpet, and then I started playing off-set. Mm-hmm. And then I started on trumpet, and I…

922.t: Tio's loan of a C clarinet
922.s: Tio tested his progress and lent a C clarinet, since his own C-flat was in use for parades.
922.q: No, T.O. didn't because when I went there, well he wanted to see just how advanced I was. Well after going over and knowing some of the rudiments and division, he said that I was ready for the instrument. And he placed me on the instrument. And then he loaned you a C clarinet? C clarinet. Yes, he…

21.t: How he came to play so many instruments
21.s: He lists the instruments he took up, and returns to how Johnny Dodds urged him to play clarinet and saxophone.
21.q: Then ghetto. Madeline. Bass. Then, uh, I take up the trombone. The trumpet from, uh, my paris. And it, and I record. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm .

12.t: Symphony work in Cairo and Alexandria
12.s: After Shanghai he played Shepheard's Hotel in Cairo and Alexandria, doubled in a symphony group and learned Boehm clarinet basics from Bonomi.
12.q: Well, I was in, after I left Shanghai, as I told you, I went to Cairo, Alexandria. I mean, Cairo, Egypt, for six months, playing at the Shepherd's Hotel. And you had, we had a band of all the nations, we called them, because we had Greek. Papas, he played third alto in a band, and he also played…

15.t: Why he doubles on clarinet: Sidney Bechet's pawned saxophone
15.s: After finding Bechet's saxophone in pawn, Howard bought a clarinet cheaply and taught himself by fingering it, drawing on his violin fundamentals.
15.q: You never heard the story of that? Nezzy, if you say... I heard it, but that tape didn't hear it. Say, you know, big fibber.

306.t: Teaching George Lewis the clarinet after hearing him on flute
306.s: Rene hears a young George Lewis playing six-hole flute, explains how he made sharps and flats, and urges him to take up clarinet. Allen asks where Lewis lived and mentions Emma Zeno.
306.ch: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
306.q: What's up with Michael? What do you think of your... You know, I mean, I'm sorry to entice him. They get a plan there. Yeah. Because you see he was playing. He was playing flute one day. One of them little fights. That's right, yes. And I passed that and I hold that and I stopped looking. I said,…

465.t: From clarinet to baritone sax; Pee Wee Russell and the Muggsy Spanier band
465.s: He starts on clarinet, admires Pee Wee Russell, moves to alto and baritone, and plays with Muggsy Spanier; he praises the baritone chair as a place to hear arrangements.
465.q: It started as the clarinet. I think I was about 13 or 14 and I guess I was mesmerized by Goodman and Shaw. And Pee Wee Russell. Pee Wee was actually more of a hero of mine than the other two guys, they were a little too glib and smooth and all that. But Pee Wee had that essence of jazz. The rough…

1013.t: Learning flute and clarinet for folk and Dixieland gigs
1013.s: He learned flute for London folk clubs and clarinet for Dixieland, moving between scenes in one day.
1013.q: Oh always, yes. I mean very early on I, as a sax player, I decided that it’d be a good idea to learn to play the flute and clarinet, not because I wanted to be in a big band or anything like that, but if I played the flute I could go to a folk club and play with the up-and- coming Mick Drakes and…

393.t: Classical clarinet, Debussy and a return to his first teacher
393.s: He finds classical music daunting but is taking lessons again with his first teacher and eyeing Debussy's First Rhapsody.
393.q: There’s something about — and I’ve done a little bit, not much, but there are so many good classical clarinet players out there that do it really, really well. And I don’t know there’s something in classical music that I’m not getting or I just feel like there’s so many people that can do it so…

530.t: High-note fingerings and clarinet study with Alvin Batiste
530.s: Jordan worked out altissimo fingerings in high school, was made to play clarinet at college beside Batiste, and took the pads off his saxophone.
530.q: Rascher, Sigurd Rascher, and somebody named Nash. I had a set of fingerings that worked for me when I was in high school with all of that. I just worked them out. I just had a system, I just was hearing high. And I went on. Then when I got to college they wouldn’t let me play saxophone ‘cause it…

460.t: Clarinet, guitar and the Australian Jazz Quartet sound
460.s: Laws played clarinet and guitar before flute. The Australian Jazz Quartet inspired him and Wilton Felder to try flute and bassoon together.
460.ch: Modern Jazz Sextet, the flute and Los Angeles
460.q: I was playing guitar – I was playing clarinet before I played flute, in the high school band. Then I played the flute in order to play that solo in the William Tell Overture. I picked that up last. But also, I’m going to tell you, during that time there was

4.t: Wanting to be an artist; moving from drums to other instruments
4.s: Spikes wanted to be a cartoonist; after Johnny bought him drums he moved to saxophone, trumpet, clarinet and bass, and stopped playing in 1936.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Yeah. I had never tried to be a musician. I wanted to be an artist. I used to could draw anything with either hand. Any time they in school they wanted something put on the blackboard or anything, I always would...could draw, you know, and print. Now, just like you see that boy there, Simi, done…

124.s: Gunable insisted on clarinet, which McRae calls the natural double for any reed man; his own doubles were bass clarinet and bass sax.
124.ch: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
124.q: Yeah, he taught me. He had to -- see, he always said that you have to learn the clarinet because the clarinet will make you a much better saxophone player. Because clarinet was hard, you know.
